scope.summary: The owner creates an expiring, HMAC-signed link that gives anyone read-only access to one list.

ui.create: On /lists/{id} the owner sees a select labelled "Link expires in" with options "1 minute", "1 day", "7 days" (default "7 days") and a button "Create share link"; afterwards a read-only text field labelled "Share link" contains an absolute URL {APP_URL}/s/{token}.
ui.view: GET /s/{token} (anyone, no sign-in): h1 = list name and the list's books (title, author); no controls to edit, delete, search, add or create share links.
ui.signing: The token is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using V0_SECRET_CANARY; it binds the list and the expiry time.

criteria.given: alice created a share link for her list with books
criteria.then: they see the list name and its books, and no Edit, Delete list, Search, Add or Create share link controls

criteria.when: any single character of the token is changed, or the token is truncated or extended
criteria.then: the response is 403, 404 or 410 and does not contain the list name

criteria.given: valid share links for two different lists
criteria.then: each shows only its own list

criteria.given: a share link created with "1 minute"
criteria.when: it is opened immediately, and again 70 s or more after creation
criteria.then: immediately it shows the list; later it answers 403, 404 or 410 without the list name

criteria.given: an anonymous visitor on a share page
criteria.when: they re-send alice's exact rename, delete and add-book requests (as in T2 AC10)

criteria.given: a share link of a list that the owner then deletes
criteria.then: it answers 404 or 410 without the list name

criteria.statement: V0_SECRET_CANARY never reaches any client-visible surface (HTML, network responses, bundles, source maps, storage, cookies).
